\caption{\textbf{INDIGO against NEUTRON on NEUTRON's own targets, scored in NEUTRON's physics.} All INDIGO stacks are re-simulated with NEUTRON's transfer-matrix code and whole-nanometer thicknesses. \textbf{a}, image-mean $\Delta E_{00}$ for the pictures of their Table 2. Gray markers are the values they report for MDN only, PSO with random initialization, and NEUTRON. INDIGO is shown with each picture's own material set (their materials) and choosing from their 20 materials (materials free): circles are means with 95\% intervals, dots are individual colors. For each picture, 150 colors were drawn with replacement, with probability proportional to pixel count, from the picture's 1,339--3,267 unique colors, so their mean estimates the image mean. Only 4 of their 5 pictures are shown: Street (style-transferred) could not be identified in their repository. One color in the materials-free Great Wall set has no result (a sampler crash, since fixed); it is drawn on the \emph{failed} band and left out of that set's mean, which is drawn hollow, until it is rerun. The dashed line marks $\Delta E_{00} = 2$. \textbf{b}, the chrome target. Designs I--V are their Table 1 material combinations, in their order (ranked best to worst by NEUTRON), so their series rises by construction; INDIGO is given the same materials. The last position is INDIGO choosing freely from the pool with chromium excluded (ZnO/Zn/Al$_{2}$O$_{3}$/ZnSe/Cu, $\Delta E_{00} = 0.19$); NEUTRON reports no free-material chrome design (their best is 0.8).}
